heuristic.applicability: Prefer when drawer_position is already below the open value, closure progress or stopping is the main uncertainty, and target_pose plus drawer_position define a stable reachable closed destination. It remains valid from early release because all 900:1330 labels are supervised, but its intended advantage is the 1140:1330 handle/closure/release interval. The observed drawer can move from about 0.300 through intermediate 0.29, 0.19, 0.08 or 0.025 values to about 0.0022.

handoff.entry_conditions: Block is inside the open or partly closed drawer, or still completing a valid release during 900:1160 overlap; target_pose and drawer_position must form a finite destination frame.
handoff.exit_conditions: Observed drawer_position below 0.025 with negligible velocity, block enclosed near z 0.063, fingers open, and TCP retreated high and clear.
handoff.failure_signatures: Predicted/observed closure response disagrees, drawer stalls above 0.025, handle contact is lost, block moves out of the cavity, destination frame is inconsistent, or IK reports large residual/limit contact.
handoff.overlap_role: All 900:1160 actions remain supervised, including release, clearance and handle acquisition; this avoids a brittle closure-only receiver despite the prior's progress emphasis.
handoff.successor_readiness: Terminal readiness is based on observed state only. Auxiliary output is representation training support and is not a success or contact predicate.

heuristic.limitations: The fixed-frame construction assumes prismatic motion along target local x and accurate target_pose/drawer_position. The auxiliary learns demonstrated response under demonstrated actions and cannot sense contact truth, external jams, a displaced handle relative to the drawer, or a block obstructing closure. It may be less responsive to local TCP perturbations than the TCP-local prior and less naturally invariant to moving-frame-relative contact than the moving-drawer prior. The auxiliary cannot prove future motion and must not be used as success. Severe fixture displacement remains subject to IK/collision feasibility.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Action dimension is 10: T_closed-relative translation 3, world rotation 6D, gripper 1. Decode recomputes T_closed from the fresh target_pose and drawer_position, constructs a world TCP target, then calls shared IK from measured q. A trainable MLP condition encoder and scalar closure-delta head are registered, optimized, checkpointed and EMA-tracked; the encoder conditions the unchanged DiffusionBackbone. encode_targets emits closure_delta = drawer_position after slot 8 minus current slot-1 drawer_position and a mask requiring both slots valid. compute_loss reports diffusion loss and weighted auxiliary prior loss separately. HL should prefer this model for partially completed closure, not infer contact merely because the auxiliary predicts motion.
heuristic.rationale: Most likely failure targeted: phase ambiguity during active closure, including entry with the drawer partly closed or failure to continue to the supplied 0.025 threshold before release/retreat. In the observed closure, drawer_position and the drawer-attached target_pose move together: target_pose.x + drawer_position stays approximately 0.125 m (for example -0.175+0.300 open and 0.123+0.002 closed). Construct a fixed closed-destination frame T_closed = T_target times a +drawer_position translation on the target local x axis. Learn translation relative to this fixed destination, world-frame rotation in continuous 6D, and gripper. Inputs include two-frame TCP/object coordinates in T_closed, drawer closure error/velocity, finger width, and qpos/qvel. Add a registered shared encoder ahead of the standard DiffusionBackbone and an auxiliary head that predicts the demonstrated drawer-position change over execution slots 1:8 from the causal condition. Its masked MSE target uses only authorized future observations during training, while inference uses no future and does not need the head output. A small auxiliary weight gives a real gradient into the same encoder used by diffusion, encouraging a progress/contact-response representation while preserving the main diffusion objective. Expected benefit is better differentiation of approach, moving closure, threshold stop, release and retreat; it is not evidence of jam recovery.
heuristic.statement: Fixed closed-destination Cartesian targets with a shared learned closure-response auxiliary

assignment.subgoal: Ensure the block is released inside the open drawer, retreat from the cavity, approach and grasp the drawer handle, push the drawer from about 0.30 m travel to below the 0.025 closed threshold, release the handle, and retreat to a clear final pose. The intended contact target after release is the drawer handle; at early overlap states the block may still be the object being lowered/released and must not be confused with the handle. Approximate exit: drawer_position about 0.0022, block enclosed at z=0.063, open fingers, TCP high and clear.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Compare decoded IK FK against the demonstrated commanded TCP and unchanged gripper. Destination-relative translation and world rotation exactly reconstruct labels apart from SO(3) Gram-Schmidt and reported IK residual; unconverged IK is not replaced.

contract.cut_relation: All actions [900,1330) in all 12 trajectories are supervised. The 260 actions [900,1160) remain true overlap with placement; the auxiliary mask never trims action diffusion supervision.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [closed-destination-frame xyz metres, world-frame TCP rotation 6D, native gripper scalar]. The destination is recomputed from each action observation for labels and the fresh current observation for decoding. Translation is transformed by the destination frame; world rotation 6D is Gram-Schmidt projected; the world target is converted only by panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh qpos. Gripper >=0 opens and <0 closes. Slots are t-1 through t+14 and execution uses 1 through 8.
contract.parameter_semantics: No high-level arguments. The fixed closed-destination frame is deterministically T_target_pose times a +drawer_position translation along target local x. Drawer units are metres. The future drawer delta is a masked training-only auxiliary label and is never an inference input or success signal.
